import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Gilbert–Pollak conjecture

The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture (1968) concerns the *Steiner ratio* of the Euclidean plane:
the ratio of the length of a Steiner minimum tree to the length of a Euclidean minimum
spanning tree, in the worst case over all finite point sets. It asserts that this ratio is
$\sqrt{3}/2$, i.e. that for every finite set of points in the plane the Euclidean minimum
spanning tree is at most $2/\sqrt{3}$ times as long as the Steiner minimum tree. The bound is
attained by the three vertices of an equilateral triangle.

A proof announced by Du and Hwang in 1990 was later found to contain a serious gap, and the
conjecture is considered open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert%E2%80%93Pollak_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [GiPo68] Gilbert, E. N. and Pollak, H. O., *Steiner minimal trees*.
  SIAM J. Appl. Math. 16 (1968), 1–29.
- [DuHw92] Du, D.-Z. and Hwang, F. K., *A proof of the Gilbert–Pollak conjecture on the Steiner
  ratio*. Algorithmica 7 (1992), 121–135.
- [IvTu12] Ivanov, A. O. and Tuzhilin, A. A., *The Steiner ratio Gilbert–Pollak conjecture is
  still open*. Algorithmica 62 (2012), 630–632.
- [IvTu14] Ivanov, A. O. and Tuzhilin, A. A., *Du–Hwang characteristic area: Catch-22*.
  [arXiv:1402.6079](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6079)
-/

namespace GilbertPollakConjecture

open Finset
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

variable {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X]

/--
The **length** of a graph `T` on a finite metric space `V` is the sum, over the edges of `T`, of
the distances between the two endpoints of the edge.
-/
noncomputable def length {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [MetricSpace V] (T : SimpleGraph V) : ℝ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  ∑ e ∈ T.edgeFinset, Sym2.lift ⟨dist, dist_comm⟩ e

/--
The length of a **minimum spanning tree** of a finite set `S` of points of a metric space `X`:
the least total length of a tree whose vertex set is exactly `S` (i.e. of a spanning tree of the
complete graph on `S`, with every edge weighted by the distance between its endpoints).

In the Euclidean plane this is the length of the shortest network of line segments connecting
the points of `S` whose endpoints all lie in `S`, i.e. the Euclidean minimum spanning tree.
-/
noncomputable def mstLength (S : Finset X) : ℝ :=
  sInf {length T | (T : SimpleGraph S) (_ : T.IsTree)}

/--
The length of a **Steiner minimum tree** of a finite set `S` of points of a metric space `X`:
the infimum of the total length of a tree whose vertex set is a finite set containing `S`.
The vertices not in `S` are the *Steiner points*. Equivalently, this is the infimum of
`mstLength T` over all finite sets `T` of points with `S ⊆ T`.
-/
noncomputable def smtLength (S : Finset X) : ℝ :=
  sInf {mstLength T | (T : Finset X) (_ : S ⊆ T)}

/--
The **Steiner ratio** of a metric space `X`: the infimum, over all finite sets `S` of at least two
points of `X`, of the ratio of the length of a Steiner minimum tree of `S` to the length of a
minimum spanning tree of `S`.

This is the convention of the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems (a number at most `1`); the
Wikipedia article on the conjecture uses the reciprocal convention (the supremum of the
ratio of the minimum spanning tree length to the Steiner minimum tree length).
-/
noncomputable def steinerRatio (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] : ℝ :=
  sInf {smtLength S / mstLength S | (S : Finset X) (_ : 2 ≤ #S)}

/-- The length of a graph is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
theorem length_nonneg {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [MetricSpace V] (T : SimpleGraph V) :
    0 ≤ length T := by
  classical
  refine Finset.sum_nonneg fun e _ => ?_
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | _ u v => exact dist_nonneg

/-- The length of a minimum spanning tree is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
theorem mstLength_nonneg (S : Finset X) : 0 ≤ mstLength S := by
  refine Real.sInf_nonneg ?_
  rintro _ ⟨T, -, rfl⟩
  exact length_nonneg T

/-- The length of a Steiner minimum tree is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
theorem smtLength_nonneg (S : Finset X) : 0 ≤ smtLength S := by
  refine Real.sInf_nonneg ?_
  rintro _ ⟨T, -, rfl⟩
  exact mstLength_nonneg T

/-- A Steiner minimum tree is no longer than a minimum spanning tree (take no Steiner points). -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
theorem smtLength_le_mstLength (S : Finset X) : smtLength S ≤ mstLength S := by
  refine csInf_le ⟨0, ?_⟩ ⟨S, subset_rfl, rfl⟩
  rintro _ ⟨T, -, rfl⟩
  exact mstLength_nonneg T

/--
**Gilbert–Pollak conjecture.** For every finite set $S$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the
Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $S$ is no longer than $2/\sqrt{3}$ times the length of the
Steiner minimum tree of $S$:
$$\operatorname{MST}(S) \le \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \operatorname{SMT}(S).$$

Equivalently, the Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane is $\sqrt{3}/2$; the three vertices of an
equilateral triangle show that the constant $2/\sqrt{3}$ cannot be improved. For sets with fewer
than two points both lengths are $0$ and the inequality is trivial.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51 90]
theorem gilbert_pollak_conjecture (S : Finset ℝ²) :
    mstLength S ≤ 2 / √3 * smtLength S := by
  sorry

/--
**Gilbert–Pollak conjecture**, stated as in the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems: the Steiner
ratio of the Euclidean plane is $\sqrt{3}/2$, i.e.
$$\inf_{S} \frac{\operatorname{SMT}(S)}{\operatorname{MST}(S)} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},$$
the infimum being over all finite sets $S$ of at least two points in the plane.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51 90]
theorem gilbert_pollak_conjecture.variants.steinerRatio_eq :
    steinerRatio ℝ² = √3 / 2 := by
  sorry

end GilbertPollakConjecture

/-- The length of the straight-line tree `G` whose vertices belong to the finite point set `s`. -/
noncomputable def treeLength (s : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)))
    (G : SimpleGraph s) : ℝ :=
  ∑ e ∈ G.edgeFinset,
    Sym2.lift ⟨fun x y : s ↦ dist x.1 y.1, fun x y ↦ dist_comm x.1 y.1⟩ e

/-- The length of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree of the finite point set `s`. -/
noncomputable def mstLength (s : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : ℝ :=
  sInf {l : ℝ | ∃ G : SimpleGraph s, G.IsTree ∧ l = treeLength s G}

/--
The length of a Steiner minimum tree for `s`, defined as the infimum of the minimum spanning
tree lengths of finite point sets containing `s`. The additional points are the Steiner points.
-/
noncomputable def steinerTreeLength (s : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : ℝ :=
  sInf {l : ℝ | ∃ t : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), s ⊆ t ∧ l = mstLength t}

/--
The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture: for every finite set `s` of at least two points in the Euclidean
plane, the Euclidean minimum spanning tree has length at most $2/\sqrt{3}$ times the length of a
Steiner minimum tree. Equivalently, with the reciprocal convention from the list entry, the
Steiner ratio is $\sqrt{3}/2$; the equilateral triangle attains this bound.
-/

theorem gilbert_pollak_conjecture :
    ∀ s : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), 2 ≤ s.card →
      mstLength s ≤ (2 / Real.sqrt 3) * steinerTreeLength s := by
  sorry

end GilbertPollakConjecture

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Gilbert–Pollak conjecture

For a finite set $S$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the *Euclidean minimum spanning tree*
of $S$ is the shortest tree whose vertex set is exactly $S$, with edges the straight
segments between its endpoints. A *Steiner minimum tree* of $S$ is the shortest tree whose
vertex set contains $S$; the extra vertices are called *Steiner points*. Equivalently, its
length is the infimum of the minimum spanning tree lengths of all finite supersets of $S$.

The *Steiner ratio* of the Euclidean plane is the infimum, over all finite point sets with at
least two points, of the ratio of the length of a Steiner minimum tree to the length of a
minimum spanning tree. (The Wikipedia article uses the reciprocal convention, the supremum of
the ratio of the minimum spanning tree length to the Steiner minimum tree length, which
equals $2/\sqrt{3}$ under the conjecture.)

The three vertices of an equilateral triangle of unit side length have a minimum spanning
tree of length $2$ and a Steiner minimum tree of length $\sqrt{3}$, so the Steiner ratio is
at most $\sqrt{3}/2$. The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture (1968) states that this is the worst
case: the Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane is exactly $\sqrt{3}/2$, i.e. for every finite
point set the minimum spanning tree is at most $2/\sqrt{3}$ times as long as the Steiner
minimum tree. A proof published by Du and Hwang in 1990 was later found to have a serious
gap, and the conjecture is regarded as open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Gilbert–Pollak conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert%E2%80%93Pollak_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [E. N. Gilbert, H. O. Pollak, *Steiner minimal trees*, SIAM J. Appl. Math. **16** (1968),
  1–29](https://doi.org/10.1137/0116001)
- [A. O. Ivanov, A. A. Tuzhilin, *The Steiner ratio Gilbert–Pollak conjecture is still open*,
  Algorithmica **62** (2012), 630–632](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00453-011-9508-3)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace GilbertPollakConjecture

variable {P : Type*} [MetricSpace P]

open scoped Classical in
/--
The total length of a graph `G` on a finite set of points of a metric space: the sum, over
the edges of `G`, of the distances between their two endpoints.
-/
noncomputable def totalLength {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [PseudoMetricSpace V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℝ :=
  ∑ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, Sym2.lift ⟨dist, dist_comm⟩ e

/--
The length of a minimum spanning tree of a finite set of points `S` in a metric space: the
least total length of a tree whose vertex set is exactly `S`.
-/
noncomputable def mstLength (S : Finset P) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ T : {T : SimpleGraph S // T.IsTree}, totalLength T.1

/--
The length of a Steiner minimum tree of a finite set of points `S` in a metric space: the
infimum, over all finite sets `S'` containing `S`, of the length of a minimum spanning tree
of `S'`. The points of `S'` not in `S` are the Steiner points.
-/
noncomputable def steinerLength (S : Finset P) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ S' : {S' : Finset P // S ⊆ S'}, mstLength S'.1

/--
The Steiner ratio of a metric space `P`: the infimum, over all finite sets `S` of at least two
points of `P`, of the ratio of the length of a Steiner minimum tree of `S` to the length of a
minimum spanning tree of `S`.
-/
noncomputable def steinerRatio (P : Type*) [MetricSpace P] : ℝ :=
  ⨅ S : {S : Finset P // 2 ≤ S.card}, steinerLength S.1 / mstLength S.1

/--
The minimum spanning tree of a two-point set consists of the single segment joining the two
points.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem mstLength_pair [DecidableEq P] {x y : P} (h : x ≠ y) : mstLength {x, y} = dist x y := by
  sorry

/--
The vertices of an equilateral triangle of unit side length have a minimum spanning tree of
length $2$: two sides of the triangle.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5 52]
theorem mstLength_equilateral {x y z : ℝ²}
    (hxy : dist x y = 1) (hyz : dist y z = 1) (hxz : dist x z = 1) :
    mstLength {x, y, z} = 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The vertices of an equilateral triangle of unit side length have a Steiner minimum tree of
length $\sqrt{3}$: the three segments from the vertices to the centroid.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 52]
theorem steinerLength_equilateral {x y z : ℝ²}
    (hxy : dist x y = 1) (hyz : dist y z = 1) (hxz : dist x z = 1) :
    steinerLength {x, y, z} = √3 := by
  sorry

/--
**The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture.**

For every finite set $S$ of at least two points in the Euclidean plane, the length of a
Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $S$ is at most $2/\sqrt{3}$ times the length of a Steiner
minimum tree of $S$. Equivalently, the Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane is $\sqrt{3}/2$,
since the equilateral triangle shows that the ratio cannot be larger.

The restriction to at least two points only excludes the degenerate case in which both
lengths are $0$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem gilbert_pollak_conjecture (S : Finset ℝ²) (hS : 2 ≤ S.card) :
    mstLength S ≤ 2 / √3 * steinerLength S := by
  sorry

/--
**The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture**, stated as in the Wikipedia list of unsolved problems:
the Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane is $\sqrt{3}/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 52]
theorem gilbert_pollak_conjecture.variants.steinerRatio_eq : steinerRatio ℝ² = √3 / 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane is at most $\sqrt{3}/2$, as shown by the vertices
of an equilateral triangle.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 5 52]
theorem steinerRatio_le : steinerRatio ℝ² ≤ √3 / 2 := by
  sorry

end GilbertPollakConjecture

Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane. The *Euclidean minimum spanning tree*
of $P$ is a shortest network of line segments connecting the points of $P$ whose endpoints all
belong to $P$. A *Steiner minimum tree* of $P$ is a shortest network of line segments connecting
the points of $P$ that may also use additional endpoints, called *Steiner points*. The
*Steiner ratio* of the Euclidean plane is the infimum, over all finite point sets $P$ (with at
least two points), of the ratio of the length of a Steiner minimum tree of $P$ to the length of a
Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $P$. (Some authors, including the Wikipedia article on the
conjecture, use the reciprocal convention and call the supremum of the reciprocal ratios the
Steiner ratio.)

The equilateral triangle of unit side length has a minimum spanning tree of length $2$ and a
Steiner minimum tree of length $\sqrt{3}$, so the Steiner ratio is at most $\sqrt{3}/2$.
The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture states that this example is the worst case, i.e. that the Steiner
ratio of the Euclidean plane equals $\sqrt{3}/2$. Equivalently, for every finite set of points in
the Euclidean plane, the Euclidean minimum spanning tree is no longer than $2/\sqrt{3}$ times the
Steiner minimum tree. A proof published by Du and Hwang in 1990 was later found to contain a gap,
and the conjecture is considered open.

- [Wikipedia, Gilbert–Pollak conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert%E2%80%93Pollak_conjecture)

tree length), is equal to $\sqrt{3}/2$. The three vertices of an equilateral triangle show that the
ratio $\sqrt{3}/2$ is attained, so the open part of the conjecture is the inequality.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Gilbert–Pollak conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert%E2%80%93Pollak_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- Gilbert, E. N.; Pollak, H. O. (1968), _Steiner minimal trees_, SIAM Journal on Applied
  Mathematics, 16 (1): 1–29.
-/

namespace GilbertPollakConjecture

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/-- The total Euclidean length of a graph `G` whose vertices are placed at the points `p v` of the
plane: the sum, over all edges of `G`, of the distance between the two endpoints of the edge. -/
noncomputable def totalLength {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²) : ℝ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  ∑ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => dist (p u) (p v), fun _ _ => dist_comm _ _⟩ e

/-- The length of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree of a finite set `P` of points in the plane:
the least total length of a tree whose vertex set is exactly `P` and whose edges are the straight
line segments between their endpoints.

If `P` has fewer than two points this is `0`. -/
noncomputable def mstLength (P : Finset ℝ²) : ℝ :=
  sInf {L | ∃ T : SimpleGraph P, T.IsTree ∧ L = totalLength T (↑)}

/-- The length of a Steiner minimum tree of a finite set `P` of points in the plane: the length of
the shortest network of straight line segments connecting the points of `P`, where the network is
allowed to use additional vertices (Steiner points) not in `P`. This is the infimum of the lengths
of the Euclidean minimum spanning trees of all finite sets `Q` containing `P`. -/
noncomputable def smtLength (P : Finset ℝ²) : ℝ :=
  sInf {L | ∃ Q : Finset ℝ², P ⊆ Q ∧ L = mstLength Q}

/-- The total length of a graph is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
lemma totalLength_nonneg {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²) :
    0 ≤ totalLength G p :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun e _ => Sym2.inductionOn e fun _ _ => by simp

/-- The graph with no edges has total length `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
lemma totalLength_bot {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (p : V → ℝ²) : totalLength ⊥ p = 0 := by
  unfold totalLength
  exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun e he => by simp at he

/-- The length of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
lemma mstLength_nonneg (P : Finset ℝ²) : 0 ≤ mstLength P :=
  Real.sInf_nonneg fun _ ⟨T, _, hL⟩ => hL ▸ totalLength_nonneg T _

/-- The empty set has no spanning tree, so its minimum spanning tree length is `0` by convention. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 51]
lemma mstLength_empty : mstLength ∅ = 0 := by
  have : {L | ∃ T : SimpleGraph (∅ : Finset ℝ²), T.IsTree ∧ L = totalLength T (↑)} =
      ∅ := by
    ext L
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
    rintro ⟨T, hT, -⟩
    exact hT.isConnected.nonempty.elim fun x => Finset.notMem_empty _ x.2
  rw [mstLength, this, Real.sInf_empty]

/-- The minimum spanning tree of a single point has length `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 5 51]
lemma mstLength_singleton (x : ℝ²) : mstLength {x} = 0 := by
  have : {L | ∃ T : SimpleGraph ({x} : Finset ℝ²), T.IsTree ∧ L = totalLength T (↑)} =
      {0} := by
    ext L
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨T, -, rfl⟩
      rw [Subsingleton.elim T ⊥, totalLength_bot]
    · rintro rfl
      exact ⟨⊥, ⟨SimpleGraph.connected_bot_iff.2 ⟨inferInstance, inferInstance⟩,
        SimpleGraph.isAcyclic_bot⟩, (totalLength_bot _).symm⟩
  rw [mstLength, this, csInf_singleton]

/-- The length of a Steiner minimum tree is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
lemma smtLength_nonneg (P : Finset ℝ²) : 0 ≤ smtLength P :=
  Real.sInf_nonneg fun _ ⟨Q, _, hL⟩ => hL ▸ mstLength_nonneg Q

/-- A Steiner minimum tree is no longer than a Euclidean minimum spanning tree. -/
@[category API, AMS 5 51]
lemma smtLength_le_mstLength (P : Finset ℝ²) : smtLength P ≤ mstLength P :=
  csInf_le ⟨0, fun _ ⟨Q, _, hL⟩ => hL ▸ mstLength_nonneg Q⟩ ⟨P, subset_rfl, rfl⟩

/-- **Gilbert–Pollak conjecture.** For every finite set $P$ of points in the Euclidean plane, the
length of the Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $P$ is at most $2/\sqrt{3}$ times the length of
the Steiner minimum tree of $P$. That is, the Steiner ratio of the Euclidean plane is
$\sqrt{3}/2$ (the value attained by the vertices of an equilateral triangle). -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51 90]
theorem gilbert_pollak_conjecture (P : Finset ℝ²) :
    mstLength P ≤ 2 / √3 * smtLength P := by
  sorry

/-- The **Steiner ratio** of the Euclidean plane: the infimum, over all finite sets $P$ of at least
two points in the plane, of the ratio of the length of a Steiner minimum tree of $P$ to the length
of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree of $P$.

Note that the Wikipedia article on the conjecture uses the reciprocal convention (the supremum of
the ratio of the minimum spanning tree length to the Steiner minimum tree length), for which the
conjectured value is $2/\sqrt{3}$. -/
noncomputable def steinerRatio : ℝ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ P : Finset ℝ², 2 ≤ P.card ∧ r = smtLength P / mstLength P}

/-- **Gilbert–Pollak conjecture**, stated as the value of the Steiner ratio of the Euclidean
plane: the Steiner ratio is $\sqrt{3}/2$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51 90]
theorem gilbert_pollak_conjecture.variants.steinerRatio_eq : steinerRatio = √3 / 2 := by
  sorry

end GilbertPollakConjecture

No cardinality hypothesis on P in the main theorem: the source says 'every finite point set', and for |P| ≤ 1 both sides are 0 so the inequality holds trivially and the mathematical content is unchanged.

/-!
# Gilbert–Pollak conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Gilbert–Pollak conjecture*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert%E2%80%93Pollak_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace GilbertPollakConjecture

/-- The sum of the Euclidean lengths of the edges of a finite simple graph in the plane. -/
noncomputable def euclideanGraphLength {points : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))}
    (G : SimpleGraph ↥points) : ℝ :=
  ∑ e ∈ G.edgeFinset,
    Sym2.lift ⟨fun p q : ↥points ↦
      dist (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), dist_comm⟩ e

/-- The length of a Euclidean minimum spanning tree on a finite set of points. -/
noncomputable def minimumSpanningTreeLength
    (points : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : ℝ :=
  sInf {length : ℝ | ∃ T : SimpleGraph ↥points,
    T.IsTree ∧ length = euclideanGraphLength T}

/-- The length of a Steiner minimum tree, allowing any finite set of additional points. -/
noncomputable def steinerMinimumTreeLength
    (points : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) : ℝ :=
  sInf {length : ℝ | ∃ larger : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
    points ⊆ larger ∧ length = minimumSpanningTreeLength larger}

/--
The Gilbert–Pollak conjecture: for every finite set of at least two points in the Euclidean
plane, the Euclidean minimum spanning tree has length at most $2/\sqrt{3}$ times the length of
the Steiner minimum tree. Equivalently, under the reciprocal convention used by the cited
list entry, the Steiner ratio is $\sqrt{3}/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 51]
theorem gilbert_pollak_conjecture :
    ∀ points : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)), 2 ≤ points.card →
      minimumSpanningTreeLength points ≤
        (2 / Real.sqrt 3) * steinerMinimumTreeLength points := by
  sorry

end GilbertPollakConjecture
